notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (none found). §1985:VII.4.5.2 prints the sequential REWRITE as REWRITE record-name-1 [ FROM identifier-1 ] [ END-REWRITE ]: no INVALID KEY phrase, no other word. The superset rule rewriteStatement accepts it, SequentialIoBinder.BindRewrite resolves record-name-1 (qualified or not) to its file and binds the FROM operand, and almost everything the later format adds is refused at --std 85 (each probed): FROM literal-1 and FROM a figurative constant by VisitRecordFromPhrase (COBOL0871), FILE file-name-1 by DeclinedFilePhrase (COBOL1706), RETRY by VisitRetryPhrase and WITH [NO] LOCK by VisitRecordLockPhrase (COBOL0900), INVALID KEY and NOT INVALID KEY on a sequential file by BindRewrite through ScreenForbiddenPhrase (COBOL1720), AT END, a second FROM, a missing record-name and a file-name operand by the parser or the resolver; FROM a function-identifier (Amendment 1) and END-REWRITE inside an IF compile and run. One thing the 1985 format does not print compiles at 85: the word RECORD after record-name-1. rewriteStatement is REWRITE (recordName | FILE fileName) RECORD? and no pass asks the edition, so REWRITE R RECORD FROM W and REWRITE R RECORD compile and run; the word is the later format's (§2023:14.9.35.2 prints RECORD, not underlined, after the braces). It is the mechanism the indexed row 1985-FMT-IX.4.6.2 records for the same grammar rule. The witness runs REWRITE R FROM W END-REWRITE on a sequential file and reads the replaced record back.

next.reason: §1985:VII.4.5.2, the sequential REWRITE, is 'REWRITE record-name-1 [FROM identifier-1] [END-REWRITE]' with no INVALID KEY phrase. §2023:14.9.35.2 is one REWRITE format for every organization; it accepts the 1985 form with the same meaning, and §2023:14.9.35.3 SR2 ('Neither the INVALID KEY phrase nor the NOT INVALID KEY phrase shall be specified for a REWRITE statement that references a file with sequential organization') keeps the 1985 sequential restriction. But it adds 'FILE file-name-1', 'FROM literal-1', the retry-phrase and WITH [NO] LOCK, all refused by the 1985 format: wider, no exception condition, CHANGED.
